---
title: "Analysing edge cases that break fitting"
output: html_document
date: "2025-07-16"
editor_options: 
  chunk_output_type: console
---

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
dat = readRDS("data/edge_cases/CRC_edge_beta.rds")

ebp = readRDS("data/edge_cases/CRC_edge_ebp.rds")

summary(dat$Value_orig[dat$disease == "Adenoma"])
summary(dat$Value_orig[dat$disease == "CRC"])
summary(dat$Value_orig[dat$disease == "Control"])

# Reset s.t. Control appears in the middle to compare with CRC + Adenoma
dat$disease = factor(dat$disease, c("CRC", "Control", "Adenoma"))

summ <- as.data.frame(dat) %>%
    filter(Value_orig != 0) %>%
    group_by(disease) %>%
    summarise(
        Min   = min(Value_orig),
        Q1    = quantile(Value_orig, 0.25),
        Median= median(Value_orig),
        Mean  = mean(Value_orig),
        Q3    = quantile(Value_orig, 0.75),
        Max   = max(Value_orig),
        .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    tidyr::pivot_longer(-disease, names_to = "stat", values_to = "value")

# Plot with summary lines
ggplot(dat[dat$Value_orig != 0, ], aes(x = Value_orig, fill = disease)) +
    geom_histogram(position = "identity", alpha = 0.4, bins = 250) +
    geom_vline(data = summ, aes(xintercept = value, color = stat),
               linetype = "dashed", size = 0.6, show.legend = TRUE) +
    facet_wrap(~ disease, ncol = 1) +
    theme_minimal() +
    labs(x = "Value_orig", y = "Count",
         color = "Statistic") +
    scale_color_manual(values = c(
        Min    = "black",
        Q1     = "blue",
        Median = "red",
        Mean   = "darkgreen",
        Q3     = "blue",
        Max    = "black"
    )) + theme(text = element_text(size = 16))

# Reset the s.t. Control is now ref
dat$disease = factor(dat$disease, c("Control", "CRC", "Adenoma")) 

fit_basic = glmmTMB::glmmTMB(
  formula = as.formula('Value ~ disease + age + sex + BMI'),
  ziformula = as.formula('~ disease + age + sex + BMI'),
  data = dat, 
  priors = ebp@priors_df,
  family = glmmTMB::beta_family(link = "logit")
)

summary(fit_basic)

# This is the model we fit
fit_rand_int = glmmTMB::glmmTMB(
  formula = as.formula('Value ~ disease + age + sex + BMI + (1 | study)'),
  ziformula = as.formula('~disease + age + sex + BMI'),
  data = dat,
  priors = ebp@priors_df,
  family = glmmTMB::beta_family(link = "logit")
)

summary(fit_rand_int)


# priors can be recomputed, or weak ones can be used - but this converges and the p-value is sufficiently low
fit_interact = glmmTMB::glmmTMB(
  formula = as.formula('Value ~ disease*study + age + sex + BMI'),
  ziformula = as.formula('~disease + age + sex + BMI'), # kept it like this to ensure convergence
  data = dat,
  # priors = ebp@priors_df, 
  family = glmmTMB::beta_family(link = "logit")
)

summary(fit_interact)

# This one does not converge! p-value is low, but we shouldn't trust it
fit_rand_intNslope = glmmTMB::glmmTMB(
  formula = as.formula('Value ~ disease + age + sex + BMI + (1 + disease | study)'),
  ziformula = as.formula('~disease + age + sex + BMI'),
  data = dat,
  priors = ebp@priors_df,
  family = glmmTMB::beta_family(link = "logit")
)

summary(fit_rand_intNslope)

```
